SIG AF (Special Interest Group for Atrial Fibrillation) is a professional medical organization in Denmark dedicated to improving the quality of care for patients with atrial fibrillation. The group serves as a key collaborative partner for [[regionernes-kliniske-kvalitetsudviklingsprogram|Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram]], focusing on the development, dissemination, and implementation of clinical guidelines for patient education, as well as ensuring accurate medical coding using the BFKB system [^src1]. 

Within the broader context of national healthcare quality monitoring, SIG AF addresses systemic barriers to structured patient education. National quality indicators have revealed significant regional disparities, with only specific units like Midtklyngen meeting the national standard of providing structured education to at least 50% of newly diagnosed patients within their first year. To overcome challenges such as the lack of harmonized educational offerings and the underutilization of specific coding practices, SIG AF drives implementation initiatives aligned with European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines [^src1]. In 2023, the group was involved in developing a guideline for patient education content based on these ESC standards [^src1].

Looking to the future, SIG AF has outlined strategic priorities to enhance both the delivery and documentation of care. The organization plans to increase its focus on disseminating educational programs, promoting their recommended content, and ensuring the correct coding of these educational interventions nationwide [^src1]. Furthermore, SIG AF collaborates directly with the [[afdk-anbefalinger-for-patientundervisningen|AFDK Anbefalinger for patientundervisningen]] to spread and implement specific patient education recommendations across the country [^src2]. The group's expertise is also integrated into broader analyses of systemic challenges, working alongside clinical professionals and patient representatives to improve long-term monitoring and educational outcomes [^src2].
